sub_chapter_briefs.title: The Logbook
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Mara sits at her shortwave station at dusk, running her nightly scan of the dead bands and recording silence in her logbook — entry 2,547 — with the same methodical precision she has used every night for seven years.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: Mara sits at her shortwave station at dusk, running her nightly scan of the dead bands and recording silence in her logbook — entry 2,547 — with the same methodical precision she has used every night for seven years.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 1 — Ordinary World: establishing the hero's routine and the texture of her diminished life
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: The fortified farmhouse — a converted two-storey brick building on the edge of a dead suburb, windows bricked to sill-height, antenna mast on the roof, a single oil lamp illuminating the ground-floor radio room
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Quiet, methodical, hollowed-out — the discipline of a person who has replaced feeling with procedure
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Grounds the reader in the post-Cascade ordinary world: civilization is gone, the airwaves are silent, and Mara's logbook of that silence is both her purpose and her prison — Stage 1 baseline established

sub_chapter_briefs.title: What the Cascade Left
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: A trader named Coll arrives at the farmhouse gate to collect a repaired hand-crank generator; their brief, transactional exchange reveals the shape of the world — barter economy, Reclamation Authority patrols on the eastern roads, three settlements within a day's walk all shrinking — and Mara's place in it as a useful, solitary, trusted-but-not-known figure.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: A trader named Coll arrives at the farmhouse gate to collect a repaired hand-crank generator; their brief, transactional exchange reveals the shape of the world — barter economy, Reclamation Authority patrols on the eastern roads, three settlements within a day's walk all shrinking — and Mara's place in it as a useful, solitary, trusted-but-not-known figure.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 1 — Ordinary World: the social and political landscape of the post-Cascade world shown through lived interaction, not exposition
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: The farmhouse gate — a reinforced steel frame set into a low stone wall, late-afternoon light, the dead suburb visible beyond: overgrown lots, collapsed rooflines, a water tower with a hand-painted RA insignia that someone has partially scratched out
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Wary, efficient, faintly sardonic — Mara is good at this world even though she does not love it
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Introduces the Reclamation Authority as ambient threat and establishes the barter economy Mara operates within — the ordinary world has rules and dangers that will later be disrupted by the signal

sub_chapter_briefs.title: Dani's Watch
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: After Coll leaves, Mara repairs a pocket watch by lamplight — her private ritual — and the work pulls her into a memory of her brother Dani: his voice on a handheld radio the last time she heard it, asking when she was coming back, and her answer that she needed two more days to find a replacement oscillator crystal; she never made it back in time.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: After Coll leaves, Mara repairs a pocket watch by lamplight — her private ritual — and the work pulls her into a memory of her brother Dani: his voice on a handheld radio the last time she heard it, asking when she was coming back, and her answer that she needed two more days to find a replacement oscillator crystal; she never made it back in time.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 1 — Ordinary World: the hero's wound — the unresolved grief and guilt that defines her inner life and will be tested by the journey
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: The farmhouse kitchen — a worktable cleared of everything except the watch, a loupe, a row of tiny tools, the oil lamp; outside the window, full dark and wind in dead trees
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Grief held at arm's length through craft — the memory surfaces not as breakdown but as a familiar ache she has learned to work around
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Plants the core wound: Mara chose equipment over her brother and he died. This guilt is the psychological engine of the Hero's Journey — the thing she must ultimately reckon with. ESCALATION SEED: Mara's belief that she prioritises signals over people will be tested, pressured, and finally broken across the novel. Starts here (small, private). Reappears under pressure in Chapter 4 (Harrow Country) when she learns Dani's settlement file was processed by the RA. Explodes in Chapter 6 (The Inmost Cave) when she discovers Aldric Senn's identity and must choose between the signal and confronting what was done.

sub_chapter_briefs.title: 2,547 Nights of Nothing
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: Mara returns to the radio room for her final scan of the night; she reads back through three pages of her logbook — all silence, all notation, all the same — and we understand that she has been listening for something she no longer believes exists; she writes the night's final entry, closes the book, and sits for a long moment with her hand on the receiver before switching it off.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: Mara returns to the radio room for her final scan of the night; she reads back through three pages of her logbook — all silence, all notation, all the same — and we understand that she has been listening for something she no longer believes exists; she writes the night's final entry, closes the book, and sits for a long moment with her hand on the receiver before switching it off.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 1 — Ordinary World: the hero's longing — the thing she wants but has stopped hoping for, which the Call to Adventure will directly answer
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: The radio room — shortwave receiver on a salvaged steel desk, antenna leads running up through a sealed conduit in the ceiling, the logbook open under lamplight, a hand-drawn frequency chart pinned to the wall with seven years of annotations
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Exhausted hope — not despair, but the specific tiredness of someone who keeps doing the thing anyway, without knowing why
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Completes the ordinary world portrait: Mara is competent, isolated, grieving, and still listening. The reader now knows exactly what she hopes for and what she fears — which means Chapter 1's signal will land with full weight

sub_chapter_briefs.title: Static
sub_chapter_briefs.beat: In the last minutes before sleep, Mara hears something — not a signal, not yet, just a faint asymmetry in the static on 7.850 MHz, a texture that is almost pattern; she tells herself it is ionospheric noise, writes nothing in the logbook, and goes to bed; the final image is the receiver's needle resting just off zero in the dark, trembling.
sub_chapter_briefs.brief: In the last minutes before sleep, Mara hears something — not a signal, not yet, just a faint asymmetry in the static on 7.850 MHz, a texture that is almost pattern; she tells herself it is ionospheric noise, writes nothing in the logbook, and goes to bed; the final image is the receiver's needle resting just off zero in the dark, trembling.
sub_chapter_briefs.arc_beat: Stage 1 — Ordinary World / threshold of Stage 2 — Call to Adventure: the ordinary world's last moment, with the first ghost of disruption already present
sub_chapter_briefs.setting: The radio room, then the farmhouse stairwell — darkness, the receiver left on standby, the antenna mast visible through a gap in the brickwork against a starless sky
sub_chapter_briefs.emotional_tone: Unease beneath exhaustion — something has shifted that she is not ready to name; the reader feels it even if Mara does not
sub_chapter_briefs.connects_to_book_arc: Bridges directly into Chapter 1 (The Carrier Wave): the asymmetry Mara dismisses tonight will resolve into a full encrypted signal at 2 a.m. — the Call to Adventure. The prologue ends not on silence but on the first tremor of what is coming, hooking the reader forward.
